# Results -- Study 360 (NAAIM-Exposure) on the real weekly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: join the
**weekly NAAIM Exposure Index** (active managers' reported equity exposure, 0-200%)
to **SPY total-return** closes; at each weekly survey date *t*, the observed
exposure predicts the SPY return earned over week *t+1* (one-week execution lag).
The contrarian claim: low (managers in cash) -> higher next-week return; high
(managers all-in) -> lower. **Total return on both legs** (SPY `auto_adjust=True`),
so a timing rule that sits in cash is charged its forgone dividends. As-of
**2026-06-22**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (naaim) |
|--------|--------|-------|---------------------|
| NAAIM Exposure Index (weekly, free since-inception spreadsheet, naaim.org) + SPY total return (yfinance) | 2006-07-05 -> 2026-06-10 | 1,040 weeks | `b887999dd648` |

NAAIM range over the sample: **-3.6 .. 120.6** (mean 67.3). Unconditional weekly SPY
return **+0.232%/wk (+12.0%/yr)**, HAC *t* = +3.42 (n = 1,040) -- the bar any
conditional signal must beat.

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* -- the NAAIM file is the **current
> vintage**, not strictly point-in-time (the series has had minor historical
> revisions), and the survey is a noisy weekly print; any edge is an **upper bound**
> on the live, real-time tradable version. *Tradability* -- 20 years, one venue
> (SPY), weekly rebalance.

## The signal -- direction is contrarian, magnitude is not significant

Among weeks bucketed by the *prior* NAAIM exposure tercile, the next-week SPY return:

| Regime (prior exposure) | Next-week return | HAC *t* | n |
|-------------------------|------------------|---------|---|
| **Low (managers in cash)** | **+16.2%/yr** | +1.92 | 347 |
| Mid | +11.3%/yr | +2.15 | 346 |
| **High (managers all-in)** | **+8.6%/yr** | +2.49 | 347 |
| **Low - High gap** | **+7.6 pp/yr** | -- | -- |

The **direction is the contrarian one** -- weeks following manager pessimism beat
weeks following manager euphoria by ~7.6 pp/yr. But note that **every** regime,
including the all-in one, still earns a clearly *positive* forward return: high
exposure is not a sell, just a *smaller buy*.

## Headline tests -- the contrarian edge is WEAK

| Test | Estimate | HAC *t* |
|------|----------|---------|
| Long-short (long cash-regime / short all-in-regime) | +2.52%/yr on active weeks | **+0.81** |
| Predictive regression slope (ret ~ std. exposure) | **-0.040%/sd** | **-0.40** |
| Regression R-squared | ~0.03% | -- |

The regression **slope sign is correct (negative = contrarian)** but **|t| < 1**,
and the R-squared is ~0.03% -- weekly exposure explains essentially none of
next-week variance. By the desk rubric (REAL needs HAC *t* >= 2 on the real tape),
this is **WEAK**: the literature supports the sign, this tape cannot certify a
robust magnitude.

## Tradability -- the overlay LOSES to buy-and-hold

| Strategy (total return, 5 bps one-way) | Return | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|----------------------------------------|--------|-------------|---------|
| Long/flat contrarian overlay (sit out the all-in regime) | **+8.68%/yr** | +0.57 | +2.72 |
| **Buy-and-hold SPY (total return)** | **+12.04%/yr** | +0.73 | -- |

The overlay is in-market 67% of weeks and nets **+8.7%/yr**, well *below*
buy-and-hold's **+12.0%/yr**: managers go all-in precisely during the meat of bull
markets, so "fading the pros" sits out the weeks you most need. Same shape as the
retail survey ([Study 257 -- AAII](../../257-aaii-sentiment/)): a directionally-true
contrarian tilt that never pays for the upside it skips.

## Sub-period analysis -- direction stable, significance not

| Period | Low regime | High regime | Low *t* | n |
|--------|-----------|-------------|---------|---|
| 2006-2012 | +6.3%/yr | +1.2%/yr | +0.34 | 339 |
| 2013-2019 | +22.5%/yr | +12.2%/yr | +2.28 | 364 |
| 2020-2026 | +22.0%/yr | +12.0%/yr | +1.37 | 337 |

Low > high in **every** sub-period (robust *direction*), but the low-regime t-stat
clears 2 only in the 2013-2019 slice -- and on the current-vintage tape.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds a contrarian edge when planted

On the deterministic synthetic weekly tape (`data.synthetic_weekly`) the predictive
regression recovers a planted contrarian loading and reads ~zero on the null:

| Planted edge | Regression slope HAC *t* |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| 0.000 (null) | **-0.37** (~0) |
| 0.004 | **-6.12** (significant negative) |

The engine works; the real NAAIM tape simply carries a weak, untradeable version.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The contrarian *direction* is real and stable across all
  sub-periods (cash-regime +16.2%/yr vs all-in +8.6%/yr next week, gap +7.6 pp/yr),
  but the headline long-short HAC *t* = +0.81 and the predictive-regression slope
  *t* = -0.40 both fall far short of the *t* >= 2 bar; R-squared ~0.03%. Literature
  (NAAIM commentary; the broader sentiment-timing work) supports the sign but not a
  robust, tradable magnitude. The series is current-vintage, not point-in-time, so
  even this is an upper bound. Verdict: **WEAK**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A long/flat contrarian overlay nets **+8.7%/yr**,
  *below* buy-and-hold's **+12.0%/yr**: sitting out the all-in regime skips the core
  of bull markets. The "edge" never pays for the missed upside. Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Pros smarter than retail? -- NOT SUPPORTED.** The whole pitch is that NAAIM is
  *professional* positioning, so fading it should beat fading a retail survey. It
  doesn't: the active-manager gauge gives the **same** weak, untradeable contrarian
  tilt as the individual-investor AAII survey ([Study 257](../../257-aaii-sentiment/)).
  Knowing what the pros *do* is no more bankable than knowing what retail *thinks*.
